message.content:
The drive from San Francisco to Los Angeles is roughly **380–400 miles** (about 610–640 km) along the I‑5 corridor. Under normal conditions—average speeds of 55–65 mph (90–105 km/h) and no major stops—the trip takes about **6 hours**.  

In practice, actual travel time can vary:

| Factor | Effect on Time |
|--------|----------------|
| **Traffic** (especially near the Bay Area, Sacramento, or the Los Angeles metro) | Adds 30 min–2 hrs |
| **Speed limits** (I‑5 is 70 mph/110 km/h in many sections) | Keeps average speed high |
| **Stops** (fuel, food, rest) | Adds 15–30 min per stop |
| **Weather** (fog, rain, snow) | Can slow traffic or close lanes |

So, expect **6 hours** under ideal conditions, but plan for **7–8 hours** if you’re traveling during rush hour or through congested areas.
